morning_first: Monday morning. Under the door, a letter from the editor before you.
morning_letters: Monday morning. The paper is out, and {n} letter(s) came under the door.
morning_none: Monday morning. Nothing under the door. Last week's ledger is on the desk.
tip_door_night: Go out · somewhere to keep watch
press_wait: The press waits for Sunday. Keep the week's material in the notebook till then.
slept_in: You stayed up too late and slept till noon. The morning is gone. More than two late nights a week will do that.
first_week: Week one. Your predecessor said the postman is reliable: take the door on the right and find him at the post office. What you learn goes in the notebook.
first_tuesday: The left-hand drawer holds the informant's address. Three dollars buys a few questions about someone.
evening: It's dark. Listen at the tavern, keep watch somewhere (a late night), or go to bed.
saturday: Saturday. Someone may call tonight; tomorrow is Sunday, layout and press day.
hint_lead: ★ Lead: {from} said to find {who}, who is at {where} right now.
hint_unverified: {n} matter(s) in the notebook, {u} item(s) not yet confirmed.
informer_day_only: The informant only meets by day.
informer_broke: The informant wants three dollars. The drawer doesn't have it.
informer_pick: Who should the informant ask about?
informer_note: Costs $3 and one action. The informant is accurate, but can be bought. Only people you have met or heard of are listed.
hint_lead_self: ★ Lead: {who} wrote that they have more to tell, and is at {where} right now.
first_wednesday: The red stamps by each item in your notebook: one per person or record, and three means confirmed. Unconfirmed items can still run, but the town remembers when you get it wrong.
hint_lead_vouch: ★ Lead: {who} saw what you are looking into first-hand and has not been asked yet; at {where} right now.
